boundary_suggestions.concept_transition: Total capacitor energy to energy per unit volume
boundary_suggestions.after_suggestion:
In this ideal model, the electric field occupies mainly the volume $Sd$ between the two plates.
Dividing the total stored energy in expression (8-44) by this volume gives the energy per unit volume, or energy density:

boundary_suggestions.concept_transition: Electrostatic energy-density validity to alternating electric-field storage and its limits
boundary_suggestions.after_suggestion:
For an alternating electric field, under the same dielectric conditions, the instantaneous field strength can be used to calculate the instantaneous stored energy density of the electric-field part.
An alternating electromagnetic field may also store energy in its magnetic field. The magnetic-field part must be calculated separately; the electric-field expressions above must not be treated as the total electromagnetic-field energy.
These two expressions cannot be applied directly to a dielectric that is dispersive or nonlinear, or has significant losses.

translation_preservation_notes.preserved_scope: Stationary charged bodies; electrostatic interaction energy rather than all energy of the bodies; reversible dielectric polarization included; an appropriate dielectric model required.

Ideal parallel plates; negligible fringing; approximately uniform field; vacuum or homogeneous, linear, isotropic, nondispersive dielectric with negligible losses; fixed dielectric properties and plate geometry.

Pointwise electrostatic energy density within the stated material limits; instantaneous alternating electric-field energy under the same conditions; magnetic energy is additional; no direct application to dispersive, nonlinear or significantly lossy media.

Initially neutral electrically floating metal slab; no grounding, power connection or plate contact; full overlap coverage; two vacuum gaps; negligible fringing; slab thinner than plate separation; both gaps positive; equal and opposite induced charges; series-capacitance solution retained; position independence conditional on the model; thickness dependence and zero-thickness limit retained.

Like-polarity connections; power supplies disconnected before connection; isolated conductor combinations with no external charge exchange; fixed capacitances; wire capacitance neglected; real transients decay before a steady state is assumed; full charge-conservation solution and final voltage retained; electric-field energy need not be conserved; heat and radiation account for decreased field storage; no automatic settling assumed in a model with neither dissipation nor radiation.
